newsitem.title: USA: KIWI fails to get financing ok, to end flights.
newsitem.headline: KIWI fails to get financing ok, to end flights.

text.p: Kiwi International Air Lines said it would suspend flights Tuesday night after the bankrupt budget airline failed to obtain financing it needed to continue operating.

Kiwi said it had interest from several potential investors, including a $2 million proposal from Remington Products Co. owner Victor Kiam II, but no firm offer materialised during a hearing in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Newark, N.J., the company said.
"No one wanted to pony up," said company spokesman Rob Kulat.

The Newark, N.J.-based airline, with 1,200 employees and $40 million in debt, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection from creditors Sept. 30. The company said it was taking the action due to its debt load, a slowing of passenger traffic after the deadly crash of a ValuJet airliner May 11 and Kiwi's own partial shutdown.

Until Tuesday night, Kiwi had been running a reduced schedule of 24 daily flights to New York, Chicago and Atlanta. Before the bankruptcy filing it had been flying 63 flights a day, with service to Las Vegas, Florida and Bermuda in addition to the other cities.
Kiwi took its name from the flightless New Zealand bird.
